Definition: comparative of a compound of G2095 and G2873; better for toil, i.e. more facile:--easier.
BiblicalUsage: eukopṓteros is a plain word for easier. In Matthew 9:5, the text says "For whether is easier." In Matthew 19:24, the text says "It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle."
TheologicalSignificance: I take eukopṓteros to mean that salvation is God's work from first to last — we receive it, we do not achieve it. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Healing of the Paralytic; The Rich Young Ruler
